scenario.name: Microsoft Defender for Identity, CERT-FR & MITRE DFIR — Kerberos Golden Ticket Forgery Forensics (EID 4768 / 4769)
scenario.overview: Imagine a giant theme park where every visitor must first visit the front admission booth to receive an official stamped day wristband before any ride operator will issue a ride pass. Having stolen the park master ink stamp earlier, an intruder prints an impossible ten-year VIP wristband at home and walks straight up to an inner ride gate without ever passing through the front booth, immediately tripping forensic auditors who spot a VIP ride pass with zero front-gate admission record. In this scenario (T1558.001, Microsoft Defender for Identity, CERT-FR & MITRE DFIR, Kerberos Golden Ticket Forgery Forensics , EID 4768 / 4769), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: offline TGT Forgery with Stolen krbtgt Key, then orphaned TGS-REQ, then target Host LogonType 3 with Synthetic. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Offline TGT Forgery with Stolen krbtgt Key, then Orphaned TGS-REQ, then Target Host LogonType 3 with Synthetic, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 10 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Offline TGT Forgery with Stolen krbtgt Key & Pass-the-Ticket LsaCallAuthenticationPackage
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1558.001 - Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket)
stages.description: Sitting quietly at a compromised desk away from the park entrance, the intruder presses the stolen master ink stamp onto a homemade VIP wristband claiming ten years of executive authority and slips it straight into their local memory pocket. On a compromised workstation, the attacker runs kerberos::golden /domain:corp.local /sid:S-1-5-21-3819201 /aes256:<krbtgt_key> /user:ghost_admin /id:500 /groups:512,513,518,519,520 /ptt. Because the TGT is encrypted locally using the stolen krbtgt key and injected directly into LSASS via LsaCallAuthenticationPackage (KERB_SUBMIT_TICKET_MESSAGE), zero AS-REQ traffic (EventID 4768) is sent to the Domain Controller (logged in Sysmon Event 10 with Technique=Offline Golden Ticket Forgery + Pass-the-Ticket , /ptt, ForgedUserAndRid=ghost_admin , RID 500 Domain Admin, InjectedDefaultLifetime=10 Years , Mimikatz default EndTime, StartTime, KdcAsReqBypassed=True , No EventID 4768 generated so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes mimikatz "kerberos::golden /domain:corp.local /sid:S-1-5-21-3819201 /aes256:4f91a82b... /user:ghost_admin /id:500 /ptt" (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1558.001 during "Offline TGT Forgery with Stolen krbtgt Key & Pass-the-Ticket LsaCallAuthenticationPackage" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). Next, the follow-up artifact LsaCallAuthenticationPackage(KerbSubmitTicketMessage) injects forged TGT into current LogonId runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , LsaCallAuthenticationPackage, KerbSubmitTicketMessage injects forged TGT into current LogonI so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1558.001 during "Offline TGT Forgery with Stolen krbtgt Key & Pass-the-Ticket LsaCallAuthenticationPackage" , On a compromised workstation, the attacker runs kerberos::golden /domain:corp while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ rubeus.exe golden /aes256:4f91a82b... /user:ghost_admin /id:500 /domain:corp.local /sid:S-1-5-21-3819201 /ptt / ⇠#1 ACK 10) from Node ① (#1 Rubeus / Mimikatz ptt Host) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CIFS/CORP-DC01 Target Service).

stages.title: Stage 2: Orphaned TGS-REQ (Security EventID 4769 Without Preceding 4768) & PAC Validation Anomaly
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1550.003 - Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Ticket)
stages.description: Approaching the main vault service desk, the intruder flashes their homemade wristband to request a door pass. Because the ink stamp matches mathematically, the desk hands over a vault pass, yet the audit ledger immediately exposes two glaring anomalies: no front-gate entry ever existed, and the wristband expiration date stretches far beyond normal park hours. When the attacker accesses \\CORP-DC01\C$, the workstation presents the forged TGT in a KRB_TGS_REQ to CORP-DC01. The KDC decrypts the TGT with its krbtgt key and logs Security EventID 4769 (A Kerberos service ticket was requested) for TargetUserName=ghost_admin@CORP.LOCAL and ServiceName=cifs/CORP-DC01.corp.local, creating an orphaned 4769 for a principal that never authenticated via 4768 (and since Windows Nov 2021 KB5008380 PAC enhancements, mismatches between the PAC SID and SAM account trigger KDC failure 0x25 / EventID 4769 Status 0x6) (logged in WinEvent Event 4769 with EventID=4769 , Kerberos Service Ticket Requested, OrphanedTicketAnomaly=Zero preceding EventID 4768 , AS-REQ for ghost_admin, TicketEncryptionType=0x17 , RC4-HMAC Downgrade, ServiceName=cifs/CORP-DC01.corp.local so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes KDC Security EventID 4769: Account_Name=ghost_admin@CORP.LOCAL Service_Name=cifs/CORP-DC01.corp.local (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1550.003 during "Orphaned TGS-REQ , Security EventID 4769 Without Preceding 4768 & PAC Validation Anomaly" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). Next, the follow-up artifact SIEM Anomaly 1: EventID 4769 observed for ghost_admin with zero EventID 4768 in preceding 10 hours runs (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1550.003 during "Orphaned TGS-REQ , Security EventID 4769 Without Preceding 4768 & PAC Validation Anomaly" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ KRB_TGS_REQ ServiceName=cifs/CORP-DC01.corp.local AccountName=ghost_admin@CORP.LOCAL / ⇠#2 ACK 4769) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 Kerberos KDC TCP/UDP :88), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CIFS/CORP-DC01 Target Service).

steps.plainTitle: Orphaned TGS-REQ (Security EventID 4769 Without Preceding 4768) & PAC Validation Anomaly
steps.storyAnalogy: Approaching the main vault service desk, the intruder flashes their homemade wristband to request a door pass. Because the ink stamp matches mathematically, the desk hands over a vault pass, yet the audit ledger immediately exposes two glaring anomalies: no front-gate entry ever existed, and the wristband expiration date stretches far beyond normal park hours.
steps.simpleExplanation: When the attacker accesses \\CORP-DC01\C$, the workstation presents the forged TGT in a KRB_TGS_REQ to CORP-DC01. The KDC decrypts the TGT with its krbtgt key and logs Security EventID 4769 (A Kerberos service ticket was requested) for TargetUserName=ghost_admin@CORP.LOCAL and ServiceName=cifs/CORP-DC01.corp.local, creating an orphaned 4769 for a principal that never authenticated via 4768 (and since Windows Nov 2021 KB5008380 PAC enhancements, mismatches between the PAC SID and SAM account trigger KDC failure 0x25 / EventID 4769 Status 0x6) (logged in WinEvent Event 4769 with EventID=4769 , Kerberos Service Ticket Requested, OrphanedTicketAnomaly=Zero preceding EventID 4768 , AS-REQ for ghost_admin, TicketEncryptionType=0x17 , RC4-HMAC Downgrade, ServiceName=cifs/CORP-DC01.corp.local so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).

Next, the follow-up artifact SIEM Anomaly 1: EventID 4769 observed for ghost_admin with zero EventID 4768 in preceding 10 hours runs (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1550.003 during "Orphaned TGS-REQ , Security EventID 4769 Without Preceding 4768 & PAC Validation Anomaly" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline).
